# Behavioral Specification: Power Manager Fast Sequencing Module

## 1. Overview

This module performs the fast-clock-domain power-management sequencing for the system. It is responsible for bringing the system from a powered-down or reset condition into normal operation, for responding to low-power entry requests, for handling system reset requests, and for returning the system to active operation after wake-up or reset.

The module controls the following classes of behavior:

- Power-up sequencing after reset, wake, or reset-triggered reboot.
- Low-power entry sequencing, including fall-through and abort cases.
- Reset request handling and reset-triggered reboot.
- Clock enable and disable sequencing.
- Life-cycle reset and system reset sequencing.
- Boot-time initialization of OTP and life-cycle controller.
- Strap sampling after reset or power-up.
- Processor fetch enable control.

The module is not responsible for slow-clock power-domain sequencing; it coordinates with the slow-clock domain through request and acknowledgment handshakes.

---

## 2. Reset Behavior

When the module’s reset is asserted, or when power is first restored, the module shall enter its powered-down/low-power reset condition. In this condition:

- All power-domain reset requests shall be asserted for both life-cycle reset and system reset classes.
- The IP clock enable output shall be deasserted, keeping second-level IP clocks disabled.
- The processor fetch enable shall be off.
- The power-down request shall be deasserted.
- The power-up acknowledgment shall be deasserted.
- The low-power indication shall be asserted.
- The reset cause output shall report an undefined or unknown reset cause.
- Strap sampling shall be cleared so that the next power-up sequence performs strap sampling again.

This reset condition is the base state from which every power-up sequence starts.

---

## 3. Power-Up Sequence

A power-up sequence shall begin when the module is in the low-power reset condition and either:

- A power-up request is received, or
- The module is performing a reset-triggered reboot.

The power-up sequence shall be performed in the following order:

1. Enable IP clocks and wait until the clock enable status confirms that clocks are enabled.
2. Release life-cycle reset requests for all power domains and wait until the reset status confirms that the life-cycle resets are released.
3. Assert the OTP initialization request and wait until OTP initialization completes.
4. Assert the life-cycle initialization request and wait until life-cycle initialization completes.
5. Perform strap sampling. If strap sampling has not yet occurred since the last reset assertion, the strap sampling control shall be driven active so that system straps are sampled. Strap sampling shall only be performed once per reset/power-up cycle.
6. For a wake-initiated power-up, assert the power-up acknowledgment and keep it asserted until the power-up request is deasserted. For a reset-triggered power-up, the power-up acknowledgment shall not be asserted.
7. When the power-up request is deasserted, or when the reset-triggered sequence reaches the equivalent point, clear the configuration lock so that software can reconfigure power-control settings.
8. If the power-up was caused by a wake event, assert the wake interrupt indication. If it was caused by a reset event, do not assert the wake interrupt.
9. Clear the low-power indication, release the system reset requests, and set the reset cause output to “no reset.”
10. Wait until the ROM check has completed successfully.
11. Enter the active operating condition and enable processor fetch.

The module shall not enter the active condition until the ROM check has completed successfully.

---

## 4. Active Operating Condition

In the active condition:

- Processor fetch is enabled.
- IP clocks are enabled.
- The reset cause output is “no reset.”
- The low-power indication is deasserted.

From the active condition, the module shall monitor two classes of requests:

- Low-power entry requests.
- Reset requests.

If either class is asserted, the module shall:

1. Disable processor fetch immediately, so no further instructions are fetched.
2. Set the reset cause output to an undefined value while the transition is being resolved.
3. Disable IP clocks and wait until the clock enable status confirms that clocks are disabled.

If both a reset request and a low-power entry request are present at the decision point, the reset request shall take priority and the module shall follow the reset path.

Once the clocks are confirmed off, the module shall determine whether to follow the low-power entry path or the reset path.

---

## 5. Low-Power Entry

The low-power entry path is taken when the clocks have been disabled and no reset request was present at the decision point.

During the low-power entry path, the module shall perform a fall-through check. The module shall clear the software low-power hint during this fall-through phase.

### 5.1 Low-Power Fall-Through

If the low-power entry request deasserts during the fall-through phase, this means the processor has resumed operation before a power-down actually occurred. In this case, the module shall:

- Re-enable IP clocks.
- Assert the wake interrupt indication.
- Assert the fall-through indication.
- Return to the ROM check phase.
- Re-enter the active condition after the ROM check completes successfully.

The fall-through indication distinguishes this case from a normal wake from low power.

### 5.2 Idle Check and Low-Power Abort

If the low-power entry request remains asserted during the fall-through phase, the module shall check whether the following components are idle:

- OTP.
- Life-cycle controller.
- Flash.

If any of these components is not idle, the module shall not proceed with power-down. Instead, it shall:

- Re-enable IP clocks.
- Assert the wake interrupt indication.
- Assert the abort indication.
- Return to the ROM check phase.
- Re-enter the active condition after the ROM check completes successfully.

The abort indication signals that low-power entry was attempted but could not be completed because a non-idle component prevented it.

### 5.3 Low-Power Preparation

If all required components are idle, the module shall proceed with low-power entry. During this phase:

- The reset cause output shall indicate a low-power entry reset cause.
- If the main power domain is to remain powered on, the non-always-on power-domain reset requests shall remain deasserted.
- If the main power domain is to be powered off, the module shall assert reset requests for all non-always-on power domains, for both life-cycle reset and system reset classes.
- The always-on power domain shall not be reset during low-power entry.
- The module shall wait until the reset status confirms that the requested reset state is valid before proceeding.

Once the reset state is valid, the module shall:

1. Assert the power-down request.
2. Wait for the power-down acknowledgment.
3. Deassert the power-down request.
4. Enter the low-power reset condition.

In the low-power reset condition, IP clocks remain disabled, processor fetch remains off, and the low-power indication remains asserted.

If a reset request arrives after the module has already committed to the low-power entry path, the reset request shall not preempt the in-progress low-power entry. The low-power entry shall complete first. A pending reset request will then cause a new power-up/reset sequence from the low-power condition.

---

## 6. Reset Handling

Reset requests are handled in two contexts:

- Reset requests that arrive while in the active condition.
- Reset requests that arrive while in the low-power condition and cause a reset-triggered power-up.

### 6.1 Reset Request in Active Condition

When a reset request is detected in the active condition, the module shall:

1. Disable processor fetch.
2. Disable IP clocks and wait until clocks are confirmed off.
3. Clear the software low-power hint.
4. Assert all reset requests for all power domains, for both life-cycle reset and system reset classes.
5. Set the reset cause output to indicate a hardware/reset-request reset cause.
6. Wait until the reset status confirms that all resets are asserted.
7. Enter the low-power reset condition.

Because the reset request caused the module to enter the low-power reset condition, the module shall automatically begin a reset-triggered power-up sequence without waiting for an external power-up request.

During this reset-triggered power-up:

- The power-up acknowledgment shall not be asserted.
- The wake interrupt shall not be asserted.
- The normal power-up sequence of releasing life-cycle resets, initializing OTP, initializing life-cycle, and performing strap sampling shall be followed.
- At the reset-triggered power-up completion point, the configuration lock shall be cleared.
- The reset cause output shall transition to “no reset.”
- System reset requests shall be released.
- The module shall wait for successful ROM check completion.
- The module shall enter the active condition and enable processor fetch.

The reset-request inputs shall also be made available on the reset-cause recording output so the system can determine which reset source caused the reset.

### 6.2 Reset Request in Low-Power Condition

If a reset request arrives while the module is already in the low-power reset condition, the system shall generate a power-up request. The module shall treat this as a reset-triggered power-up.

In this case:

- The power-up sequence shall be the same as for a wake-triggered power-up.
- The power-up acknowledgment shall not be asserted.
- The wake interrupt shall not be asserted because the power-up cause is a reset, not a wake event.

---

## 7. Output Behavior Summary

### 7.1 Wake Interrupt

The wake interrupt indication shall be asserted when:

- A power-up request is received with a wake cause and the power-up handshake completes.
- A low-power fall-through occurs.
- A low-power abort occurs because a required component was not idle.

The wake interrupt shall not be asserted for reset-triggered power-ups.

### 7.2 Fall-Through Indication

The fall-through indication shall be asserted when a low-power entry is abandoned because the low-power entry request deasserted before power-down completed. This is not an error; it indicates that the processor resumed normal execution before entering low power.

### 7.3 Abort Indication

The abort indication shall be asserted when a low-power entry is abandoned because OTP, life-cycle controller, or flash was not idle. This indicates that the low-power entry did not complete and the system is returning to active operation.

### 7.4 Clear Low-Power Hint

The module shall clear the software low-power hint during:

- The fall-through phase of low-power entry.
- The reset shutdown path when a reset request interrupts normal operation.

This prevents stale low-power hints from causing unintended low-power entry after the current event is resolved.

### 7.5 Clear Configuration Lock

The configuration lock shall be cleared when the module completes a power-up handshake or a reset-triggered power-up sequence, just before returning to the ROM check phase. This allows software to modify power-management configuration after reset or wake.

### 7.6 Low-Power Indication

The low-power indication shall be asserted:

- During the initial reset condition.
- During low-power entry.
- While in the low-power reset condition.

It shall be deasserted when the module begins the ROM check phase after a successful power-up or reset-triggered power-up.

### 7.7 Fetch Enable

Processor fetch enable shall be off during all reset, power-up, and low-power phases. It shall only be asserted in the active operating condition.

### 7.8 IP Clock Enable

The IP clock enable output shall be:

- Deasserted in the low-power reset condition.
- Asserted during power-up after clocks are requested.
- Deasserted during low-power entry and reset before the clocks are turned off.
- Re-asserted when a low-power fall-through or abort returns the system to the ROM check phase.

The module shall not advance past a clock-enable or clock-disable phase until the clock enable status confirms that the requested clock state has been reached.

---

## 8. Reset Cause Output

The reset cause output shall report the current reset reason to the reset-status interface.

The required values are:

- “Undefined” during initial reset and during active-to-low-power or active-to-reset transitions.
- “Low-power entry” during the low-power preparation phase and until the ROM check phase after a wake.
- “Hardware reset request” during a reset-triggered shutdown and reset-triggered power-up until the ROM check phase.
- “No reset” during the active condition and during the normal ROM check phase after a wake.

---

## 9. Summary of Sequencing Rules

The module shall obey the following ordering rules:

- Do not release life-cycle resets until clocks are enabled.
- Do not start OTP initialization until life-cycle resets are released.
- Do not start life-cycle initialization until OTP initialization is complete.
- Do not perform strap sampling until life-cycle initialization is complete.
- Do not release system resets until after the power-up acknowledgment phase or the reset-triggered equivalent.
- Do not enter the active condition until the ROM check has completed successfully.
- Do not assert the power-down request until clocks are disabled and the required reset state is valid.
- Do not allow processor fetch until the active condition is reached.
